title: Pre-label TTL cache replay
scenario: Replay a request log against a TTL cache that sits in front of a model server handing out pre-labels per (task, model, locale). Publishes bump the model version and flush that model. Test 2 checks the JSON report.

verified.why_correct: `expires_at <= now` looks like the opposite boundary from get(), but it is the same rule seen from the other side: an entry is expired at exactly t + T, so purge must remove it when expires_at == now.

bugs.title: Cache key drops the locale
bugs.symptom: test_ocr_lookups fails: the 09:02:00 fetch for T01 fr-fr comes back as ('hit', 'ocr-v1@1/T01/en-us') instead of ('miss', 'ocr-v1@1/T01/fr-fr'), and the 09:04:00 fr-fr fetch also returns the en-us value.
bugs.why: The key is only (task, model), so T01's fr-fr fetch finds the en-us entry and serves the English pre-label as a hit. README rule 1 says locale is part of the identity.
hints: Look at the 09:02:00 ocr fetch. What locale was asked for, and what locale is in the value returned?
How is the cache key built for a fetch?
make_key returns (task_id, model); it needs (task_id, model, locale).
probes: Why did the bad hit disappear after the 09:06:00 publish?
The CacheEntry stores locale too. Why doesn't that protect the lookup?

bugs.title: Entry still served at its exact expiry
bugs.symptom: test_seg_lookups fails: the 09:02:30 seg-v2 fetch for T02 is a 'hit' instead of a 'miss', and the 09:03:00 fetch then flips from hit to miss.
bugs.why: seg-v2 has a 120 s TTL; the entry stored at 09:00:30 expires at 09:02:30, and the fetch at exactly 09:02:30 must miss. `<=` treats the expiry instant as still fresh, so it hits, the entry is not refreshed, and the 09:03:00 fetch then misses instead of hitting.
hints: Compare the seg fetches at 09:02:30 and 09:03:00 with the TTL for seg-v2.
Read README cache rule 3, then look at how freshness is checked on lookup.
TTLCache.get uses now <= entry.expires_at; it should be now < entry.expires_at.
probes: purge_expired uses <= and is correct. Why are the two comparisons opposite?
Why did the 09:03:00 fetch change from hit to miss, even though it isn't on a boundary?

bugs.title: last_refresh dumped via str() instead of ISO
bugs.symptom: test_last_refresh fails: every last_refresh comes out as '2026-03-02 09:15:30' (space) instead of '2026-03-02T09:15:30'.
bugs.why: The raw datetime goes into the report, and report_json's default=str turns it into '2026-03-02 09:15:30' with a space. The spec wants the ISO 'T' form that every other timestamp uses.
hints: Compare the last_refresh strings with the other timestamps in the JSON.
How does each timestamp field in build_report get turned into a string?
last_refresh needs iso(s.last_refresh) if s.last_refresh else None.
probes: Why didn't json.dumps raise on a datetime here?
Would test_last_refresh have caught this if it read build_report() instead of report_json()? What would it show?

context_qa.q: What does replay() do for each request row?
context_qa.a: For `publish` it bumps the backend version for the model and calls `cache.drop_model`. For `fetch` it builds a key with `make_key`, calls `cache.get(key, req.ts)`, and records a hit if an entry comes back. Otherwise it calls the backend, stores a new CacheEntry with `expires_at = ts + ttl`, and records a miss. Per-model counts live in ModelStats.

context_qa.q: Where does the TTL for a model come from?
context_qa.a: `load_config` reads `default_ttl_seconds` and the `ttl_seconds` map, lower-casing and trimming model names and converting values with int(). `replay` uses `ttls.get(model, default_ttl)`, so ner-v3 (no override) gets 300 seconds.
Only once, in `build_report`, at the ts of the last log row, before the snapshot is built. Lookups during the replay never call it.
task_id, model, locale, value, stored_at and expires_at. The snapshot is built from these entry fields, not from the cache keys.

context_qa.q: How is a blank locale handled?
context_qa.a: `norm_locale` returns the trimmed lower-cased value or `en-us` if that is empty. `load_requests` only applies it to `fetch` rows; publish rows get an empty locale.

context_qa.q: How does report_json differ from build_report?
context_qa.a: It calls build_report and passes the result to json.dumps with indent=2, sort_keys=True and default=str.
